ai_root_cause: Interface Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of the required VLAN 10.
ai_evidence: show vlan brief shows VLAN 10 exists | show interfaces switchport shows Fa0/2 is assigned to VLAN 20
ai_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface Fa0/2 | switchport access vlan 10 | end
expected_fault: Fa0/2 is assigned to the wrong VLAN.

ai_root_cause: VLAN 20 is missing from the allowed VLAN list on the trunk interface connecting SW1 and SW2.
ai_evidence: show interfaces trunk output indicates VLAN 20 is not in the allowed VLAN list.
ai_fix_steps: Enter interface configuration mode for the trunk interface on the switch using 'interface <interface_name>'. | Add VLAN 20 to the trunk allowed VLAN list using 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20'. | Repeat the process on the connecting trunk interface of the neighbor switch if configured identically. | Verify connectivity between hosts in VLAN 20 using ping.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is missing from the trunk allowed list.

ai_root_cause: Absence of a Layer 3 inter-VLAN routing mechanism (SVI or router-on-a-stick) to route traffic between distinct VLANs.
ai_evidence: show vlan brief demonstrates that VLANs exist | show ip route demonstrates no routes or SVIs exist for the VLANs
ai_fix_steps: Deploy a Layer 3 routing device or enable L3 features on the switch if supported. | Create SVI interfaces for each VLAN and assign appropriate IP addresses. | Enable IP routing using the 'ip routing' command if using an L3 switch. | Ensure hosts in each VLAN have their default gateway set to the corresponding SVI or router interface IP address.

ai_root_cause: Native VLAN configuration mismatch across the EtherChannel trunk interface causing STP inconsistency or port down state.
ai_evidence: show etherchannel summary shows Port-channel is down | show interfaces trunk shows native VLAN mismatch
ai_fix_steps: Access configuration mode on both switch peers for the relevant Port-channel interface. | Execute 'switchport trunk native vlan 150' on both sides to align the native VLAN configuration. | Verify port-channel recovery using 'show etherchannel summary' and 'show interfaces trunk'.
expected_fault: Native VLAN configuration is inconsistent on the Port-channel/trunk.

ai_root_cause: The PC is configured with an incorrect default gateway IP address (192.168.10.254) instead of the actual router gateway interface address (192.168.10.1).
ai_evidence: PC IP configuration gateway is set to 192.168.10.254 | Router interface IP address is 192.168.10.1
ai_fix_steps: Change the default gateway configuration on the PC to 192.168.10.1. | Test reachability from the PC to the remote network using ping.
expected_fault: PC has the wrong default gateway.

ai_root_cause: Incorrect host subnet mask configured on the PC, causing remote traffic to be misclassified as local or improperly routed instead of being forwarded to the default gateway.
ai_evidence: Router LAN interface is 192.168.20.1/24 | PC default gateway is set to 192.168.20.1 | PC can ping local devices but cannot reach remote subnets
ai_fix_steps: Reconfigure the PC subnet mask to match the network mask of 255.255.255.0 (/24). | Confirm the PC default gateway is correctly set to 192.168.20.1. | Verify connectivity from the PC to remote subnets via ping.
expected_fault: Incorrect host subnet mask prevents correct remote-network forwarding.

ai_root_cause: The client PC has no DNS server IP address configured in its IP settings, preventing hostname resolution while direct IP connectivity remains functional.
ai_evidence: Web server opens by IP address but not by hostname. | PC IP configuration shows the DNS server field is blank.
ai_fix_steps: Configure the DNS server option under the appropriate DHCP pool on the router using the 'dns-server <IP-address>' command. | If statically assigned, manually enter the primary DNS server IP address in the client PC network adapter settings. | Execute 'ipconfig /renew' on the client PC to obtain updated DNS server settings from DHCP.
expected_fault: Client has no DNS server configured.

ai_root_cause: An Access Control List (ACL) entry applied to the router is blocking DNS and HTTP traffic.
ai_evidence: DNS and HTTP fail after an ACL is applied. | show access-lists shows DNS/HTTP traffic is denied by an ACL entry.
ai_fix_steps: Modify the ACL to explicitly permit DNS (UDP/TCP port 53) and HTTP (TCP port 80) traffic from internal clients to destination services. | Apply the updated ACL configuration to the active interface.
